examples.en: My mom is very understanding.
I'm lucky to have met such an understanding teacher.
Please be a little more understanding toward your friend.
Thanks to my roommate's understanding, I live comfortably.
If people lack understanding of each other, they fight easily.

examples.ko: 부부 사이에는 서로에 대한 이해심이 필요해요.
examples.en: Between spouses, mutual understanding is needed.

explain: '이해심이 깊다/많다/부족하다'처럼 남의 사정을 헤아리고 받아들이는 마음을 말해요. 내용을 알아듣는 능력인 '이해력'과 달라요. 성격을 칭찬할 때 '이해심이 많은 사람'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 남의 사정에 이해심이 부족해요.
phrases.en: He lacks understanding for other people's situations.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남의 입장을 헤아리지 못할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone can't consider another person's position.

phrases.example: 우리 팀장님은 이해심이 넓어서 실수해도 괜찮아요.
phrases.en: Our team leader is very understanding, so mistakes are okay.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음이 넓고 잘 받아 주는 사람을 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to praise a broad-minded, accepting person.

phrases.example: 저는 이해심 있는 사람과 결혼하고 싶어요.
phrases.en: I want to marry an understanding person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 성격을 말할 때 명사를 꾸미는 형태로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form that modifies a noun when describing someone's personality.

explain_en: It is used as '이해심이 깊다/많다/부족하다' for the heart that considers and accepts other people's situations. It differs from '이해력', the ability to grasp content. To praise someone's character, say '이해심이 많은 사람'.

examples.en: I lost all affection for him because he kept breaking promises.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 직원에게 소리치는 걸 보고 정떨어져요.
examples.en: I'm turned off seeing that person yell at staff.
Don't pick only the words that turn people off.

examples.ko: 한 번 정떨어지면 다시 좋아지기 어려워요.
examples.en: Once you're turned off, it's hard to like someone again.

examples.ko: 식당이 너무 더러워서 정떨어져서 다시 안 가요.
examples.en: The restaurant was so dirty I lost all liking for it, so I won't go back.
No wonder you got turned off by that calculating behavior.

explain: '정이 떨어지다'를 줄인 말로 좋아하던 마음이 식어 싫어졌다는 뜻이에요. 사람뿐 아니라 가게나 장소에도 쓰고, 반대는 '정들다'예요.

phrases.en: I went to that shop and lost all affection for it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 줄이지 않은 원래 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The full, unshortened form.

phrases.en: Please don't say off-putting things.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 말로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to modify a noun.

phrases.en: His behavior put me off completely.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음이 식은 것을 과거형으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past tense expressing that one's affection has cooled.

explain_en: It is the short form of '정이 떨어지다' and means your fondness cooled into dislike. It works for people and also for shops or places, and the opposite is '정들다'.

examples.en: I was so shocked that I wasn't in my right mind.

examples.ko: 제정신이라면 그런 말을 못 할 거예요.
examples.en: No one in their right mind would say that.

examples.ko: 며칠 못 자서 제정신으로 일하기 힘들어요.
examples.en: After days without sleep, it's hard to work with a clear head.

examples.ko: 사고 뒤로 한동안 제정신이 아닌 것처럼 보였어요.
examples.en: After the accident, he seemed out of his mind for a while.
My friend asked if I was out of my mind.
Contacting me at this hour? Are you out of your mind?

explain: '제정신이 아니다'처럼 부정하는 말과 함께 자주 써요. 놀라거나 화나서 이성을 잃은 상태를 가리켜요. '제정신이야?'는 매우 센 말이라 친하지 않은 사이에서는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.example: 그 소식을 듣고 저는 제정신이 아니었어요.
phrases.en: I was out of my mind when I heard the news.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀라거나 화나서 이성을 잃은 상태를 말할 때 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to say someone has lost their senses from shock or anger.
phrases.en_equiv: to be out of one's mind

phrases.en: I was shocked, but I soon came to my senses.
phrases.nuance_ko: 흥분하거나 놀랐다가 다시 침착해질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone calms down after being shocked or upset.

phrases.en: It was a long while before I came to my senses.
phrases.nuance_ko: 멍하거나 혼란스럽던 상태에서 정신이 돌아올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when one's mind clears after being dazed or confused.

explain_en: It often goes with a negative, as in '제정신이 아니다' (not in one's right mind), describing someone who has lost composure from shock or anger. '제정신이야?' (Are you out of your mind?) is very harsh, so avoid it with people you aren't close to.

examples.en: I'm not joking, I'm serious.

examples.ko: 그 말이 진담인지 농담인지 잘 모르겠어요.
examples.en: I can't tell if that was serious or a joke.

examples.ko: 친구가 웃으면서 한 말에 진담이 섞여 있었어요.
examples.en: My friend's smiling remark had some seriousness mixed in.

examples.ko: 진담으로 들으면 안 돼요, 그냥 장난이에요.
examples.en: Don't take it seriously, it's just a joke.
He had the look of someone speaking seriously.

examples.ko: 선생님은 농담 속에 진담을 담아 말씀하세요.
examples.en: My teacher puts serious points inside her jokes.

explain: '농담'의 반대말이에요. '진담이에요?', '진담으로 들었어요'처럼 말해요. '농담 반 진담 반'은 장난처럼 말했지만 속마음도 들어 있을 때 써요.

phrases.example: 농담 반 진담 반으로 한 말인데 사실 가고 싶어요.
phrases.en: half joking, half serious
phrases.nuance_ko: 장난처럼 말했지만 속마음이 섞여 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said like a joke, but real feeling is mixed in.

explain_en: It is the opposite of 농담. You say 진담이에요? or 진담으로 들었어요. 농담 반 진담 반 means it was said like a joke but contains real feeling.

en: to feel hatred; to feel disgust

examples.en: My older sister recoils at the sight of bugs.
My mother can't stand lies.
I used to hate crowded places.
My friend hates karaoke, so we don't go.
They looked at me with a repelled expression.
The smell was so bad it made people recoil.

explain: '질색하다'는 '싫어하다'와 달리 몸으로 느끼는 거부감이 커요. '질색을 하다'로도 쓰고, 뜻은 거의 같아요. 사람이 주어이고, 싫은 대상은 '을/를'로 받아요.

phrases.en: My friend recoiled in disgust when she saw a cockroach.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형으로, 싫은 것을 보고 몸으로 거부감을 느꼈다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form, meaning one physically recoiled from something disliked.

phrases.en: I am a person who can't stand lies.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 것을 몹시 싫어하는 사람을 꾸며 말하는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form for someone who strongly dislikes something.
phrases.en_equiv: a person who can't stand something

phrases.en: The child avoided the bitter medicine with disgust.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-며'로 연결해서 싫어하면서 하는 행동을 함께 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Linked with -며 to describe an action done while showing disgust.

explain_en: Unlike '싫어하다', '질색하다' carries a physical sense of recoiling. '질색을 하다' means almost the same. A person is the subject and the thing disliked takes '을/를'.

examples.en: Tsk, they went without me again.

examples.ko: 쳇, 그 정도는 나도 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Humph, I can do that much too.

examples.ko: 동생은 쳇 하고 방으로 들어가 버렸어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling went 'tsk' and walked into the room.
Tsk, we lost by a hair!

examples.ko: 쳇, 공짜인 줄 알았는데 돈을 내래요.
examples.en: Tsk, I thought it was free, but they say I have to pay.
My friend went 'humph' but helped me in the end.

explain: 쳇은 기분이 안 좋거나 아쉬울 때 혼자 내는 소리예요. 화가 난 것보다는 살짝 삐지거나 못마땅한 느낌이 커요. 친한 사이에서 쓰는 가벼운 소리라서 윗사람에게 쓰면 무례해 보여요.
explain_en: This is a sound people make alone when they feel sulky or let down. It carries more mild sulking or disapproval than real anger. It is casual and used among close people, so using it toward someone older looks rude.

en: to keep silent; to say nothing

examples.en: Everyone stayed silent during the meeting.

examples.ko: 그는 질문을 받고 한참 침묵하더니 고개를 저었어요.
examples.en: After the question, he said nothing for a while and then shook his head.
I am angry, so I am not saying anything.

examples.ko: 이럴 때는 침묵하는 게 나을 수도 있어요.
examples.en: In a case like this, saying nothing may be better.
We all ate in silence.
That person will stay silent to the end.

explain: '조용하다'는 소리가 작거나 없는 상태이고, '침묵하다'는 할 말이 있을 수 있는데도 말하지 않는 것이에요. 명사 '침묵'과 함께 '침묵을 지키다', '침묵을 깨다'처럼 자주 써요.

phrases.en: That person kept silent until the end.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말하지 않고 계속 가만히 있을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for staying quiet and saying nothing.

phrases.en: My friend broke the silence first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조용하던 분위기에서 처음 말을 꺼낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when someone speaks first in a quiet moment.

phrases.en: He kept silent about the question.
phrases.nuance_ko: '계속'을 붙여서 오랫동안 말하지 않는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 계속 stresses that someone stays silent for a long time.

explain_en: '조용하다' describes a place or person with little noise; '침묵하다' is choosing not to speak even when there may be something to say. With the noun, the usual pairs are '침묵을 지키다' (keep silent) and '침묵을 깨다' (break the silence).

examples.en: Hehe, actually I ate it first.
My friend giggled sheepishly and said sorry.

examples.ko: 칭찬을 받자 아이가 헤헤 하고 웃었어요.
examples.en: When praised, the child grinned happily.

examples.ko: 헤헤, 이거 제가 직접 만든 거예요!
examples.en: Hehe, I made this myself!
I was sleepy and just kept giggling.
My younger sibling ran off to the room giggling.

explain: 헤헤는 쑥스럽거나 기분이 좋아서 장난스럽게 웃는 소리예요. '하하'는 시원하게 크게 웃을 때, '히히'는 장난스럽게 웃을 때, 헤헤는 조금 멋쩍을 때 써요. 문자나 채팅에서 많이 쓰고 격식 있는 글에는 안 써요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling ran away giggling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 헤헤보다 더 장난스럽게 웃을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a more playful laugh than 헤헤.

phrases.en: My friend laughed out loud.
phrases.nuance_ko: 헤헤보다 시원하고 크게 웃을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a bigger, hearty laugh compared to 헤헤.

phrases.en: I got praised and laughed bashfully.
phrases.nuance_ko: '헤헤'를 한 번 더 이어 붙여 웃음이 계속되는 쑥스럽고 기쁜 느낌을 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Repeating 헤헤 once more gives a continuing, shy and happy laugh.

explain_en: 헤헤 is a playful laugh when you feel shy or pleased. '하하' is a hearty laugh and '히히' a mischievous one, while 헤헤 fits a slightly sheepish moment. It is common in texts and chats but not in formal writing.

en: to cheer; to shout for joy

examples.en: When the goal went in, the crowd cheered all at once.
At the news of passing, the whole family shouted with joy.
You can hear the fans cheering all the way outside.

examples.ko: 아이들은 눈이 온다는 말에 환호하며 뛰어나갔어요.
examples.en: The kids cheered and ran outside at the news that it was snowing.
The people who were cheering suddenly went quiet.
I was surprised when the audience cheered as I greeted them on stage.

explain: 환호하다는 기쁨이나 감격으로 큰 소리를 지르며 반길 때 써요. 많은 사람이 함께 있는 상황에서 자주 쓰고, 혼자 기뻐하는 모습은 '좋아하다', '기뻐하다'로 말해요. '환호성', '환호를 보내다'처럼 명사로도 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: Cheers burst out when the game ended.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기뻐서 지르는 큰 소리를 명사로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun for the loud shout of joy.

phrases.en: The audience sent cheers to the players.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누군가에게 기쁜 마음으로 박수와 소리를 보낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when giving joyful cheers to someone.

phrases.en: The children were happy to get the present.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리를 지르지 않아도 되고, 혼자 기뻐할 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Doesn't need shouting and works when one is happy alone.

explain_en: It means shouting out loud to welcome something with joy or deep feeling. It fits scenes with many people together, while one person's happiness is usually 좋아하다 or 기뻐하다. It also appears as nouns, as in 환호성 and 환호를 보내다.

examples.en: A friend gave me this bag for free.
There's nothing in the world you get for nothing.

examples.ko: 거저 줘도 안 가질 만큼 낡은 물건이에요.
examples.en: It's so worn out that nobody would take it even if it were free.
Even though it was free, I felt bad taking it for nothing.

examples.ko: 일을 안 하고 월급을 거저 받을 수는 없어요.
examples.en: You can't get a salary for free without working.
At this price, it's almost the same as free.

explain: '공짜'와 비슷하지만 '공짜'는 명사이고 '거저'는 부사라서 '거저 주다/받다/얻다'처럼 동사 앞에 써요. 돈을 안 낼 때뿐 아니라 힘이나 대가 없이 얻을 때도 써요. '세상에 거저 되는 일은 없다'처럼 말하기도 해요.

phrases.example: 이 자리는 거저 얻은 게 아니에요.
phrases.en: I didn't get this position without effort.
phrases.nuance_ko: 노력이나 대가 없이 얻는다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means getting something without effort or cost.

phrases.en: I feel bad receiving a gift for free.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈이나 보답 없이 받을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you receive something without paying or giving back.

phrases.en: I got coffee for free at the event.
phrases.nuance_ko: '공짜'는 명사라서 '로'를 붙여 부사처럼 써요. 말할 때 더 흔해요.
phrases.nuance_en: 공짜 is a noun, so 로 makes it adverb-like; very common in speech.

explain_en: It is similar to '공짜', but '공짜' is a noun while '거저' is an adverb used before verbs, as in '거저 주다/받다/얻다'. It covers not only paying nothing but also getting something without effort or a price. People say things like '세상에 거저 되는 일은 없다'.

examples.ko: 그것참, 오늘따라 정말 신기한 일이 많네요.
examples.en: Well, what a lot of strange things happen today.
My, how did something like this happen?
Oh, what a pity. I have no words of comfort.

examples.ko: 그것참 큰일이네요. 어서 병원에 가 보세요.
examples.en: Oh dear, that's serious. Go to the hospital right away.
Well, that's odd. I'm sure I put it here.

examples.ko: 그것참, 아이가 말을 어쩜 이렇게 잘할까요?
examples.en: My goodness, how can a child speak so well?

explain: 뜻밖이거나 안타깝거나 어이없을 때 혼잣말처럼 내는 소리예요. 어떤 느낌인지는 말투에 따라 달라지고, 어른들이 많이 쓰는 말투예요. '허 참', '참 나'와 비슷하게 쓰여요.

phrases.en: Well, what on earth is going on?
phrases.nuance_ko: 어이없거나 놀랐을 때 쓰는 비슷한 혼잣말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar mutter used when you are baffled or surprised.

phrases.example: 참 나, 어이가 없어서 말이 안 나와요.
phrases.en: Seriously, I'm so speechless I can't say anything.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어이없고 기가 막힐 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you feel exasperated or dumbfounded.

phrases.en: Oh, that's too bad. It must be hard for you.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안타까운 마음을 담아 상대에게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to express sympathy to someone.

explain_en: It's a murmur-like exclamation for when something is unexpected, sad or absurd. The feeling depends on your tone, and it's a typical adult way of speaking. It's used similarly to '허 참' and '참 나'.

examples.en: You think you can win with skills like yours?

examples.ko: 네까짓 놈은 상대도 안 된다고 악당이 말해요.
examples.en: The villain says a guy like you is no match for him.

examples.ko: 네까짓 돈 따위는 필요 없다고 소리쳤어요.
examples.en: I shouted that I don't need a measly bit of money like yours.

examples.ko: 네까짓 말에 내가 흔들릴 것 같아요?
examples.en: Do you think I'd be shaken by words from the likes of you?

examples.ko: 네까짓 게 뭘 안다고 큰소리를 치냐고 화를 냈어요.
examples.en: He got angry and asked what someone like you knows to talk so big.

examples.ko: 네까짓 것쯤은 혼자서도 이길 수 있다고 큰소리쳤어요.
examples.en: He boasted that he could beat the likes of you all by himself.

explain: 상대를 아주 낮춰 보는 무례한 말이라 싸울 때나 드라마 대사에서 주로 들려요. 윗사람에게는 절대 쓰면 안 돼요. 보통 '네까짓 게', '네까짓 놈'처럼 뒤에 '것, 게, 놈' 같은 말이 붙어요.

phrases.en: What would a nobody like you know?
phrases.nuance_ko: '네까짓 것이'의 줄임말로, 상대를 깔보며 화낼 때 가장 흔히 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Short for 'that thing like you'; the most common form when scornfully angry at someone.

phrases.en: How dare a punk like you come at me?
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대가 남자일 때 쓰는 아주 거친 말이라 드라마 대사에서 많이 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: A very rough phrase for a male target, often heard in drama dialogue.

phrases.en: Who would be afraid of someone like you?
phrases.nuance_ko: '네까짓 것을'의 줄임말로, 목적어 자리에 쓰며 무시하는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Short for 'someone like you' as an object; it carries a dismissive tone.

explain_en: This is a very rude way of looking down on someone, so you mostly hear it in fights or drama lines. Never use it to someone older or higher in status. It usually comes before words like '것', '게' or '놈', as in '네까짓 게'.

examples.ko: 에라, 모르겠다. 그냥 먼저 먹어 버릴래요.
examples.en: Oh well, whatever. I'm just going to eat first.

examples.ko: 에라, 이왕 늦은 거 천천히 가요.
examples.en: Oh well, since we're already late, let's go slowly.

examples.ko: 에라, 한번 해 보기나 하자는 마음으로 신청했어요.
examples.en: I figured, oh well, why not give it a try, and applied.

examples.ko: 에라, 오늘은 공부 말고 푹 쉬어요.
examples.en: Oh well, let's skip studying today and just rest.

examples.ko: 계속 고민하다가 에라 하고 질러 버렸어요.
examples.en: After agonizing for ages, I said "oh well" and just went for it.

examples.ko: 에라, 어차피 안 될 거 포기해요.
examples.en: Oh well, it won't work anyway, so let's give up.

explain: 마음을 정하거나 포기할 때 혼잣말처럼 내뱉는 말이에요. '에라 모르겠다'처럼 굳은 말로도 써요. 친구나 가족 사이에서 편하게 쓰고, 어른 앞에서는 버릇없게 들릴 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 에라, 될 대로 돼라! 일단 해 볼래요.
phrases.en: Oh well, whatever happens! I'll just try it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결과를 걱정하지 않고 마음을 정할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when deciding to go ahead without worrying about the result.

phrases.en: Oh well, I don't care. I'll just rest today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고민하다가 포기하고 마음을 편하게 정할 때 쓰는 굳은 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A set phrase used when you stop worrying and just decide.

phrases.example: 에라, 이왕 이렇게 된 거 하나 더 시킬래요.
phrases.en: Oh well, since it's come to this, I'll order one more.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 일이 그렇게 된 김에 마음을 편히 먹고 정할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to make a relaxed decision since things have already turned out this way.
phrases.en_equiv: oh well, since it's come to this

explain_en: It is a mutter you let out when you make up your mind or give up. It also appears in the set phrase '에라 모르겠다' (oh well, whatever). Use it casually with friends and family; in front of elders it can sound rude.

examples.en: Don't cry over a trivial thing like this.
A distance this short is fine to walk.

examples.ko: 요까짓 비 정도는 우산 없이도 괜찮아요.
examples.en: A little rain like this is fine without an umbrella.
You can't give up over something this small.
Why do you begrudge such a trifling amount of money?

examples.ko: 요까짓 실수는 누구나 한 번쯤 해요.
examples.en: Everyone makes a slip like this once in a while.

explain: 하찮고 작다고 얕잡아 보는 느낌이 들어서, 자기 일에는 '별것 아니야'라는 뜻으로 쓰고 남의 것에 쓰면 무례할 수 있어요. 비슷한 말로 '이까짓', '그까짓'이 있고, 뒤에는 꼭 명사가 와요.

phrases.example: 요까짓 것쯤은 혼자 할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: I can do a little thing like this by myself.
phrases.nuance_ko: '요까짓'에 '것'을 붙여 쓰면 별것 아니라는 느낌이 더 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 'geot' makes the 'it's nothing much' feeling clearer.

phrases.example: 이까짓 비는 우산 없이 가도 돼요.
phrases.en: I can go without an umbrella in a little rain like this.
phrases.nuance_ko: '요까짓'보다 조금 덜 귀엽고 더 평범하게 들려요. 자기 일에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Sounds a bit less cute and more ordinary than 'yokkajit'. Use it for your own matters.

phrases.en: Don't worry about a trivial matter like that.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대가 말한 일을 가볍게 볼 때 쓰지만, 남의 큰 고민에 쓰면 무례할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to make light of something the other person mentioned, but it can be rude about someone's real worry.

explain_en: It carries a dismissive feeling of looking down on something small, so about your own matters it means 'it's nothing', but about someone else's things it can be rude. Similar words are '이까짓' and '그까짓', and a noun always follows it.
